title: What If You Fell Into a River Full of Piranhas? They'd Mostly Ignore You

scenes.text: What if you fell into a river full of piranhas? The movies lied to you.
To strip a 180-pound person in five minutes, experts estimate you'd need 300 to 500 piranhas, all starving, all attacking at once.
Real piranhas eat insects, seeds, fish and carrion. They swim in packs for safety, not for hunting. Caimans and river dolphins eat them.
If one bites, it usually bites once, and usually a toe or a foot. The risk rises when water is low and the fish are hungry.
The man-eater myth comes from Theodore Roosevelt in 1913. Locals netted off a stretch of river, starved the fish for days, then threw in a cow.
The documented cases of people eaten by piranhas were already dead when the fish arrived. Fall in, climb out, count your toes.

description:
What if you fell into a river full of piranhas? Experts quoted by Smithsonian estimate that stripping a 180-pound human in five minutes would take 300 to 500 starving piranhas working together. Wild piranhas mostly eat insects, fish, seeds and carrion, shoal for protection from caimans and river dolphins, and when they do bite a swimmer it is usually a single bite to a foot or toe, most often when water is low and food is scarce.
The killer reputation traces to Theodore Roosevelt's 1913 trip, when locals netted off a stretch of river, starved the fish and fed them a cow for show; in documented cases of bodies eaten by piranhas, the person had already drowned or died first.
